claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The customer's act of calling and placing an order constitutes nonverbal conduct rather than an explicit oral or written assertion, challenging whether the evidence qualifies as a statement under FRE 801(a).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a) defines a statement as an oral or written assertion or nonverbal conduct intended by the person as an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that a customer called one and placed an order

arguments.text: The evidence is offered to prove trademark confusion, which is the effect of the customer's conduct on the restaurant or the customer's state of mind, rather than to prove the truth of any asserted matter.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay only when offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted; offers for effect on listener or state of mind are non-hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that the trademarks of restaurant A and restaurant B created confusion

arguments.text: The narrative highlights the customer's belief, indicating the evidence is used circumstantially to demonstrate the customer's state of mind and the resulting confusion, a recognized non-hearsay purpose.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) excludes statements offered to show the declarant's state of mind or the effect on the listener from the hearsay definition.
arguments.evidence_span: believing it to actually be the other
